nodes.name: European beech
nodes.desc: A dominant broadleaf tree of central European forests. Its nuts (mast) are a heavy but irregular crop, and are eaten by animals.

nodes.name: Sessile oak
nodes.desc: A widespread forest oak in the area and the best recorded tree in the GBIF records. Its acorns feed deer, boar, jays and rodents.

nodes.name: Goat willow
nodes.desc: A pioneer tree of stream banks and clearings. Willow bark and shoots are food for beavers.

nodes.name: Bramble
nodes.desc: A thorny scrambling shrub of clearings and forest edges whose leaves and berries feed many animals.

nodes.name: Common nettle
nodes.desc: A nutrient-loving plant of clearings and stream edges. Its leaves are the food plant of Small tortoiseshell caterpillars.

nodes.name: Wavy hair-grass
nodes.desc: A fine grass of acidic, sandy forest soils and open ground, where it grows in tufts.

nodes.name: European roe deer
nodes.desc: A small deer that browses leaves, shoots, berries and young grass. Its fawns are vulnerable to predators.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: An omnivore that roots in the forest floor for acorns, beech nuts, roots and small animals.

nodes.name: Eurasian beaver
nodes.desc: A bark and shoot eater that cuts waterside trees such as willow. Its dams and ponds create wetlands used by many other species.

nodes.name: Bank vole
nodes.desc: A small forest rodent that eats leaves, seeds, nuts and winter bark. It is prey for foxes, martens, buzzards and wildcats.

nodes.name: Eurasian jay
nodes.desc: An omnivorous woodland bird that eats acorns, beechnuts, berries and insects, and buries acorns that help spread oaks.

nodes.name: Hazel dormouse
nodes.desc: A small arboreal rodent of hazel-rich woods that eats nuts, buds, flowers and some insects.

nodes.name: Small tortoiseshell
nodes.desc: A common butterfly whose caterpillars feed on nettle leaves; adults drink nectar from many flowers.

nodes.name: European badger
nodes.desc: An omnivore of woods and pasture. Earthworms are its main food, plus insects, fruit, carrion and small mammals.

nodes.name: European pine marten
nodes.desc: A tree-climbing woodland carnivore that takes small mammals and birds and also eats fruit.

nodes.name: Common buzzard
nodes.desc: A generalist raptor of woodland edges. Voles are a key food, and it also takes birds and carrion.

nodes.name: European wildcat
nodes.desc: A shy forest cat of the Ardennes region that hunts mainly small mammals and ground birds. Hybridisation with house cats is reported as low in Luxembourg.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: A flexible predator and scavenger of woods and fields that eats small mammals, birds, carrion and fruit.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light that reaches the forest floor in clearings and leaf-fall seasons drives plant growth.

nodes.name: Rain and mild climate
nodes.desc: Regular rainfall in the Ardennes edge keeps streams and soils moist for forest growth.

nodes.name: Sûre river and lake
nodes.desc: The Upper Sûre reservoir and its streams supply wet ground for willows and shelter for beavers.

nodes.name: Sandstone soil
nodes.desc: Acidic, sandy soils over Luxembourg sandstone, with crags and gorges, support beech and oak forest.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi, bacteria and soil animals that break down leaf litter, wood and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
